prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Ytterbium (이터븀) itself — the sovereign of the Ytterbium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: mid-twenties — a clear adult face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: a cool, aloof beauty; fair skin; delicate V-line face with a small, soft chin; medium-sized eyes — feline cat eyes, level outer eye corners; thin straight brows; straight narrow nose; thin lips with a defined cupid's bow; pale silver eyes with a fine steady ring of yellow light; glossy nude lips.
Body and hair: willowy and long-limbed with soft curves — a full bust, rounded hips and a slender waist build; two hair loops pinned high on the crown with no bangs, long face-framing side locks; soft bright silver hair crossed by fine threads of steady yellow light like a lattice.
Expression: attentive, steady eyes, mouth closed.
Her element, carried in her design: ytterbium: a soft, ductile, bright silvery metal named for the Swedish village of Ytterby, separated in 1878 in Geneva from erbia, with its younger sister lutetium still hidden inside it until 1907; held one by one in an egg-crate lattice of light, its atoms tick to a steady yellow laser more than five hundred trillion times a second in optical clocks so exact they would not lose a second over the age of the universe and can feel time run faster when lifted a few centimetres, the likely successor to the caesium second; squeezed hard, its electrical resistance rises, so it gauges the pressure of earthquakes and blasts; inside glass fibre it powers the invisible infrared lasers that cut steel.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — MECHA
Costume: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. Light soft bright-silver armor over a slim clear night-blue inner suit with fine deep-red seams, six small mirror-silver lattice units floating symmetrically around her and linked by thin crossing beams of steady yellow light into a glowing grid, a small clock-face core at the chest ticking with yellow light, fine lattice engraving on the small shoulder plates; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: light body armor with several small shield and drone units floating symmetrically around her. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Colours: bright soft silver, steady clock-laser yellow, faint deep-red lattice glow, clear night blue.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: year 2200, a clock-chain city that measures height with time: slender white clock towers stepped from the sea up to the mountain ridge, each holding atoms in a lattice of steady yellow laser light and comparing its beat with the others by light to map every rise of the land; a forming hall where invisible infrared fibre lasers cut steel in neat lines of sparks.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Yb) and atomic number (70) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish.
